rationale: Evidence from iteration 5 (score 403.4, best so far; kp 2.6, kd 0.6, ki 0.1, base_speed 1.2, sensors at x = -0.07 to 0.07 with y 0.05, sensor_size 0.016). Oval finishes rose to 17/20 and oval oscillation fell from 0.286 to 0.219. Line loss stays low (0.15 on the oval, 0.0 on the s-bend). Three problems remain. Oval oscillation is still just above 0.2. S-bend oscillation rose to 0.26 (from 0.213 at kd 0.45) and s-bend ended off track 19/20 with max_error 0.062. Slalom oscillation rose to 0.19 (from 0.10), which is the noise-amplification warning. The Evaluator's rule is that when oscillation stays above 0.2 at kd 0.6, change sensor geometry before adding more damping, and do not raise kd further. So I keep kd at 0.6 and make one geometry change: sensor_size 0.016 to 0.012. A smaller footprint averages less sensor noise and reads a sharper edge, which may cut the jitter the damping cannot. The span stays at +/-0.07 m, so the outer-sensor line-loss fix from iteration 4 is kept. Expected: oval and s-bend oscillation below 0.2, slalom oscillation down from 0.19, and s-bend max_error under 0.06. Risk: a narrower footprint may bring back line loss, as in iteration 0 (which used a narrower span). Hypotheses to check next: (a) steering_oscillation falls below 0.2 on the oval and s-bend; (b) line_loss_events stays near 0; (c) if the run is clean, base_speed 1.3 is the next lever for completion_time under 3 s. If the s-bend still goes off track with max_error near 0.06, test sensor y position (for example y 0.03 m). If slalom oscillation stays high, return kd to about 0.5.
